changes.location: Opening words of the interlinear addition
changes.evidence: The first group has an initial downstroke and two shoulders resembling m, followed by a looped e-like turn and strongly compressed low groups. This supports mesurant, but the internal letters and the final t cannot be separated sufficiently to exclude the shorter-group reading ou encore.
The m ends before the next t-shaped beginning; no independent terminal period is visible in that gap.

changes.location: tronqués and alleged deletion in the interlinear addition
changes.kind: deletion state (struck given live or live given struck)
changes.evidence: After the t/r-shaped beginning there is a small filled rounded o, a long low n stroke, a q loop with its own descender and the final u/e/s strokes. The tall crossing descender belongs to q in the full-size line above. I do not find an independent strike through the small word. The tiny accent over the e is not securely separable from background marks, so accented and unaccented forms remain open.
The final p has its own descending stem and short shoulder. The long stroke above and after it is the descender of g in groupes on the larger line; there is no independent terminal dot.

Following p and a small closed o, the long n stroke, a small c turn, the tall t and the u before the final e/s can be distinguished. There is no dotted i. The accent on the final e is too compressed to distinguish an attached accent from the letter stroke.

changes.location: Small isolated mark under the left bend of the interlinear guide

Two close high dark marks stand at the i position, with a third slightly lower mark nearby and another isolated dot farther left. A diaeresis is visually supported, but the surplus isolated marks prevent deciding whether every mark is intentional.

changes.location: Isolated mark to the left of Tes
changes.evidence: The enlargement shows a small solid upright stroke with a low spur. It stands apart from the letters and near their lower level; whether it is intentional punctuation or a copy mark is not settled.

A low dark mark with a left-descending point and a rightward spur is present between existent and the next word. Its location is punctuation-like, but the thick triangular shape leaves a blot/speck alternative.

There is a detached dark mark above the reduced middle vowel, but at this scale it is a compact block without a reliable left/right lean. The accented vowel is retained with its accent direction unresolved.

changes.location: Verb following que m' on the final line
changes.evidence: The crop separates an initial open o, low u/v/r strokes, a small looped e, a long n and a crossed terminal t. There is no intermediate dotted i, and the initial o lacks an e crossbar.

The first vowel is a closed horizontal oval without a distinct right-hand a stem. Two separate high marks stand over i, and the next letter is a broad low bowl with a rising right stroke, supporting v rather than r. A reduced a is still possible, so the unusual first-vowel reading is not silently normalized.

notes.text: The opening continuation says the formal group is concentrated in commutative formal groups and attributes the discovery to Dieudonné with the explicit reservation semble-t-il. No preceding-page text was consulted or supplied to complete this fragment.

The author asks about generalizing to groups in (n-cat), expects complexes of noncommutative chains, and asks which supplementary structures of the indicated crossed-oval type are needed. The explicit uncertainty words sans doute, mais lesquelles ? and the final candidates question are retained.

The author says the structures express exactly homotopy types truncated in dimension ≤ n for topological groups. The small insertion gives a bound ≤ n+1 for espaces top ponctués connexes, with uncertain opening wording and small accents. The two bounds, plus sign, chain indices and connector decorations prompted ink inspection only.

The lower paragraph connects reflections on biduality and the inserted homology to developments, some already existing and others requiring considerable work, and introduces réminiscences. The verb is read ouvrent; the following adjective retains a first-vowel uncertainty.

The handwritten author page number is 6. The archive pencil foliation is 151 and appears only in a TeX comment. The H page{150} wrapper is editorial metadata, not a page number imported into the reading.

No definite deletion was established. In the small tronqués, the prominent crossing descender belongs to the full-size word above, and the horizontal stroke belongs to the small word. Both additions and their guides are retained. The guide above As-tu ends in a blank interval and is not converted into a literal opening parenthesis.

Three isolated mark questions remain: the point under the insertion guide newly recorded here, the point left of Tes, and the possible comma after existent. Other isolated dots near the candidate word make the intentional status of its apparent diaeresis uncertain.

No proof check, independent re-proof, computation, formal certificate, mathematical re-use or refutation was performed. The checks list is empty. The observations concern ink, spelling, punctuation, indices, inequalities and graphic states.

coverage: I viewed the whole scan once for layout, then half a once and half b once in that order. I read every physical line and each agreed word/sign against the complete C and H texts, including accents, punctuation, letter endings, both dimension inequalities, all six chain objects, each of the five connectors, both interlinear additions and their guides, the separator and both page identifiers. Twelve tight crops were made with the supplied script for the places left unresolved; the three slanted-note crops were rotated 1.7 degrees and every crop was viewed once. No half was enlarged again, and no settled locus was independently re-cropped. C and H differ at the explicitly listed words and graphic states. H omits the separator and several small marks and expands the abbreviation comm; both witnesses lack an explicit reproduction of the insertion guides and omit the small point under the first guide. No external source, OCR, other page, other reader or LaTeX compilation was used. The complete reading and the report were compared for matching uncertainty and state markup before delivery.
